sections.overview: Amatitlania siquia is a freshwater cichlid native to Central America. It belongs to the convict-cichlid group, whose species boundaries remain under study.
sections.identification: Its relatively deep, laterally compressed body usually has about six diffuse dark bars, with the third more conspicuous as an oval blotch; the first bar is not forked. FishBase reports a maximum standard length of 7.9 cm for a male or unsexed specimen. A Costa Rican reserve paper illustrates a mature female of about 6.4 cm and male of about 5.3 cm standard length, local examples rather than sex-specific maxima. No reliable height, width or body-mass data were found.
sections.habitat: Its reported range extends from eastern Honduras through Nicaragua to central Costa Rica, on both Atlantic and Pacific slopes in Costa Rica. It occurs in freshwater river drainages and lakes; breeding fish have been studied at Lake Xiloá in Nicaragua.
sections.diet: Species-specific feeding observations were not available in the reviewed taxonomic reference or field studies, so a detailed diet is left undescribed.
sections.behavior: Breeding fish occupy and defend nesting territories, and experiments in Lake Xiloá found that pairs adjust territory boundaries in response to nearby landmarks.
sections.reproduction: Pairs care for eggs and free-swimming young; in a 2025 Lake Xiloá field study, broods with both parents were less often unattended and stayed in tighter shoals than those with one parent.
sections.ecology: The species is recorded across several Central American drainages, but its precise distribution depends on which populations are assigned to this taxon.
sections.conservation: The IUCN lists it as Data Deficient because its taxonomy is uncertain; the assessment notes localized threats from deforestation, pollution and interactions with non-native species, but no evidence of major range-wide decline at that time.
